At Shrewsbury, on the 31st ult. Miss Clara Eager, daughter of Capt. Lewis Eager, aged 24.
Richly endowed by nature, cultivated by education, and improved by grace, she lived greatly beloved by her acquaintance, and was universally lamented at her death.

In Perry, Me. Mr. Daniel Bugbee, aged 15.

In Bristol, Mr. William Gibbs, aged 80.

In Waterford on the 31st ult. Mrs. Elizabeth Jewett, wife of Deacon Stephen Jewett, aged 64.

Obituary notices are too often only the vehicles of unmeaning panegyric; but to let character of so much worth and so many endearing domestic qualities go to the grave without a memento of its distinguishing virtues, would be to withhold from society an exemplary model, too seldom found, to pass unnoticed.

Mrs. Jewett was naturally possessed of an amiable unassuming mind, tranquil temper, sincere heart and tender affection, which were early seasoned and aptly harmonized by the plastic power of divine grace. At the age of 15, she made public profession of her faith in Christ, and her succeeding character was a continual evidence of the operative nature and spirituality of her belief in the principles of the gospel. As a wife she was distinguished for every excellency; as a mother, she was affectionate and faithful; as a Christian, she was devout, humble and thankful; as a friend, sincere and sympathizing; and as a neighbor, amiable, kind and obliging. In her habitation, the stranger found home of hospitality, the way-worn traveller table of comforts, a heart of benevolence; and suffering indulgence the extended arm of charity. It may dramatically be said that she died without enemies, and that her uniform equanimity and mildness enabled her to admonish others of every inconsistency with effect, and to silence the tongue of slander without offence. She has left an aged partner in mourning, but she has left her shining lights to direct him in the decisions.
